tier_reason: First-party README tables vs Apple Accelerate cblas_sgemm/cblas_dgemm on a named CPU (Apple M5) with public benchmark code (examples/vs_accelerate.rs, interleaved best-of-12) and flags in build.rs (-mcpu=apple-m4 -ffp-contract=fast -O3) and Cargo.toml (opt-level 3, thin LTO), but neither the Apple clang nor the rustc version is stated (only MSRV 1.97), so not A under the rustc-version precedent.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Unpacked strided GEMM vs Accelerate on Apple M5, TF/s: f32 512^3 1.97 vs 1.61, 1024^3 2.34 vs 2.03, 4096^3 2.14 vs 2.07, 4096x512x512 2.29 vs 1.94, 16384x512x512 2.30 vs 2.00; Accelerate leads at 256^3 (1.50 vs 1.67) and 2048^3 (2.04 vs 2.14). f64 ahead at every shape: 256^3 0.46 vs 0.44, 512^3 0.58 vs 0.46, 1024^3-4096^3 0.55 vs 0.52, tall shapes 0.61 vs 0.52. f16 (Accelerate has no f16 path; compared with upcast + sgemm + downcast): 1024^3 3.83 vs 1.40, 2048^3 4.32 vs 1.70, 4096x11008x4096 3.32 vs 1.89. Dispatch latency (us/call, f32): Accelerate cblas_sgemm is faster at every square size 8^3-256^3 (e.g. 128^3 3.2 vs 7.9 packed SME); packed SME wins the 1x4096x4096 decode shape (634 vs 836).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: C kernels (csrc/, arm_sme.h) built by build.rs through the cc crate with -mcpu=apple-m4 -ffp-contract=fast -O3; M5-only TUs add +sme-f16f16/+sme-b16b16/+sme-f64f64/+sme-i16i64 target features behind a runtime probe. Rust release profile opt-level=3, lto="thin"; rust-version 1.97 (MSRV). Apple clang and rustc versions not stated. examples/vs_accelerate.rs: 3 warm-up calls each plus a 60-call clock warm-up, then 12 interleaved passes of 40 iterations (4 for large shapes), best per-call time kept for both backends.
corrections.caveats: Baseline is Apple Accelerate, not OpenBLAS/MKL/Eigen/BLIS, so it is off the category's usual incumbents (Accelerate may itself use the SME/AMX unit). Wins are small and mixed for f32 (Accelerate leads at 256^3 and 2048^3, and has lower per-call latency for every size up to 256^3); f64 margins are 5-26%; the large f16 margin is against an upcast-to-f32 path because Accelerate has no f16 GEMM. Some f16 cells come from the candle adapter or the inference_value example rather than vs_accelerate. Apple Silicon M4+ on macOS only (scalar reference fallback elsewhere); the kernels are C behind Rust bindings and use both the P- and E-cluster SME units via GCD. First-party, best-of-N timing, constant-valued inputs, brand-new repo (first commit 2026-08-03) with 0 stars.

notes: All record numbers appear in the README's 'vs. other backends' table; claimed_speedup extended with the other shapes, f64 rows and the dispatch-latency table where Accelerate wins small sizes. The benchmark is fair in shape (both write preallocated C, interleaved rounds). Kernels are C (csrc/*.c with arm_sme.h) wrapped in a Rust crate, so the language field could read 'C, Rust'. Apache-2.0 OR MIT, 0 stars, last commit 2026-09-30 confirmed.
